analysis.title: Global Market Outlook, November 2026: Transitioning to mid-cycle
key_insights: Standard Chartered trims global equities from Overweight to Core (Neutral) and is now Neutral on both stocks and bonds, with gold Overweight. Reasons: near-term event risks (US mid-terms on 3 November, possible renewed US strikes on Iran), high earnings expectations and a higher cost of capital.
Brent is cited well above USD 110/bbl on Iran tensions, despite significant ongoing crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

Higher US bond yields combined with high AI-sector earnings expectations raise the risk of an expectations reset. Debt-financed capex is taking a larger share of total capex. The bank estimates 40% of 2027 AI capex will be debt-financed.

The caution comes from the risk of an expectations repricing, not an expected economic slowdown. US outlook remains well supported and the bank does not expect Fed hikes to make policy overly restrictive.

The bank's quant stock-bond model score fell to -2 (range -5 to 5), a modest equity Underweight. Historically a -2 score is associated with flat to slightly negative returns. The model cut equity weight to 36% from 68%. Drivers are stretched valuations, weaker fundamentals and weaker technicals.

Technical driver of the quant model: the share of equity markets above their 200-day moving averages fell below 60% (the detailed table cites 47%, down from above 80% in August), the first sub-60% reading since January 2025.

Preferred equity regions remain the US and Asia ex-Japan (AxJ), which are expected to have the highest 2027 earnings growth among major regions. India is upgraded to Overweight for non-AI, domestically driven growth. Taiwan stays Overweight. South Korea and China are Core, ASEAN is Underweight.
Japan and Europe ex-UK stay Core as regional diversifiers, backed by financials. UK stays Underweight for limited exposure to growth sectors.

Sector views: US IT, financials, materials and healthcare Overweight. US Communication Services was cut to Neutral and US Healthcare raised to Overweight on 12 October. Europe ex-UK Industrials cut to Neutral because energy-cost shocks and supply-chain pressure outweigh fiscal support. Financials are Overweight in the US, Europe ex-UK and Japan.

Opportunistic equity ideas: closed Global Semiconductors (+8.1%), MSCI Taiwan (+10.0%), US Communication Services (+1.9%) and Global Power & Electrification (-6.5%) as a tactical cut to tech exposure, not a fundamental change. Opened MSCI Switzerland (29 Oct) and US Healthcare (12 Oct). Open ideas: Global High Dividend, Japan Banks, Euro area Banks.

US equity 12-month forward P/E has fallen to 19x from 22x at the start of the year on higher rates and worries about debt-funded growth. Global equity returns are expected to moderate from the 15-20% annualised range of recent years but stay positive.

12-month index targets: S&P 500 8,400 (9% upside), Nasdaq 100 32,400 (10%), Euro Stoxx 50 6,580 (6%), FTSE 100 11,170 (4%), Hang Seng 24,600 (7%), Nifty 50 25,000 (9%), Nikkei 225 68,500 (6%), based on 29 Oct closes.

Fixed income is Core overall. Underweight DM government bonds on term-premium risk. Overweight EM USD government bonds. DM IG and HY corporates, EM local-currency and Asia USD bonds are Core. The bank prefers corporate over government debt and limits duration to 3-7 years.

The 10-year US Treasury yield is in a range last seen in 2007. US yields retraced after a sharp bear steepening in September and early October. Real yields are expected to stay elevated for six months and yields to stay rangebound near term.

Five near-term drivers for US yields: the 3 November mid-terms (Democratic sweep bond-supportive, Republican sweep bearish for bonds), Fed communication, the 4 November Treasury quarterly refunding (reduced long-end issuance would compress long-end yields), softening auction demand and foreign repatriation, and Middle East oil risk.

Credit: DM IG spreads have widened from lows but stay near historical tights (OAS 93.2bp vs 111.2bp 5-year average per the chart). DM HY spreads are at roughly a six-month high (343.8bp vs 372.2bp 5-year average). The CCC tier is the focal point, with yields near the high-15% range and spreads near a four-year high.

AI-related IG issuance exceeds USD 250bn in 2026, weighing on the long end. Hyperscalers are turning to private markets for funding. Concern centres on funding pressure at AI neocloud companies, which the bank views as idiosyncratic for now. The US HY default rate remains below trend and HY all-in yields are above 8%.

EM USD bonds: yield pick-up of nearly 3ppt over DM peers (EM USD yield 6.8% vs 5-year average 6.6%, spread over DM 2.9ppt per the chart). Lula's surprise win in Brazil raises fiscal and political risk for LATAM. The EM USD benchmark is less exposed to oil shocks than the local-currency benchmark.
Bond opportunistic ideas: bullish US TIPS, AAA-rated CLOs, US HY and AUD corporates. Closed EU bank AT1 (+2.0%), US utilities corporate hybrids (+0.5%) and US 10-year government bonds (+1.7%).

Fed: held at 3.75-4.00% in October after hiking in September for the first time since 2023. The bank expects 25bp hikes in December and in H1 2027 to a peak of 4.25-4.50%, then a cut in Q3 2027. Money markets price another 56bp of hikes over 12 months, so the bank's path is more dovish than the market.

Fed, ECB and BoJ all hiked in September, a first for the same month, and all paused in October. The bank expects the Fed to hike twice more, the ECB once more (to 2.75% in December) and the BoJ three more times by June 2027 (to 2.00%). Markets price more than 60bp of ECB hikes over 12 months.
Macro scenarios: soft landing 45% (core), no landing 30%, downside 25%. Recession risk is raised to 15% and stagflation cut to 10%, with low risk of oil sustained above USD 120/bbl.

US data: Q3 annualised GDP growth 3.4%, October composite PMI 57.6, core PCE 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y (matching estimates). 2026 consensus GDP growth is 2.3% (from 2.1%) and 2027 is 2.2%. Consensus core PCE is 3.2% in Q4 2026 falling to 2.4% by Q4 2027.
Euro area: Q2 GDP grew 1.2% y/y, October manufacturing PMI 52.4, September headline inflation 3.8% y/y and core 2.5%. French fiscal stress and high energy costs are the key risks.

China: September manufacturing PMI 50.1 and non-manufacturing 50.2, exports +36.3% y/y, record trade surplus of USD 133.5bn, CPI 0.9% y/y, PPI 5% y/y (highest since 2022). PBoC cut a key rate by 25bp to 1.5%. The bank expects no policy rate cut this year and 2026 growth at the low end of the 4.5-5.0% target.

Japan: BoJ held at 1.25% in October after a September hike. Core-core inflation is 2.4% and expected toward 3% in Q1 2027. The BoJ plans to triple the pace of ETF sales from January 2027. Two government-appointed board members dissented on the September hike, and the two most hawkish members leave in July 2027.

Gold stays Overweight. The bank trims 3- and 12-month targets to USD 4,350/oz and 4,700/oz, and sees a strong base above USD 4,000/oz. It calls the recent pullback liquidity-driven. Support comes from EM central bank demand, led by China, and a softer USD ahead. Speculative positioning near May lows leaves room for inflows.

Oil: WTI forecasts unchanged at USD 100/bbl (3m) and USD 80/bbl (12m). Freight costs are at multi-year highs, diesel has outpaced crude (diesel index 179.2 vs WTI 141.9, Jan-25=100), and the bank sees threats to production infrastructure and thin emergency buffers.

FX: 3-month DXY forecast raised to 101 from 100.20, and 12-month kept at 98.50, with a 101-103 range expected. September payrolls slowed to 29,000 from 133,000, unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1% and wage growth eased to 3.0%. These temper expectations of aggressive Fed tightening.

The quant regime model puts bear-market probability at 4.2% for the S&P 500 and 7.7% for MSCI AC World, up from 0.9% and 6.4% in September. The US recession probability is 25% within six months, up from 21%. The market diversity indicator flags reversal risk in MSCI Europe Real Estate (down over 12% from its August peak) and MSCI China Industrials (down over 19%).

Total Portfolio Approach analysis: the Foundation Balanced portfolio carries AI ecosystem risk of 19.7% vs 32.6% for a 60/40 portfolio, and Foundation+ carries 18.8%. Foundation+ shows an annualised return of 10.7%, volatility of 9.2% and downside capture of 49.6%. The equity beta of hedge fund multi-strategy is about 0.15-0.20.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth remains the main driver, with 16% global earnings growth projected for 2027. US Q3 earnings point to a robust economy, and AI is seen as a structural growth theme.
tension_points.bear_case: Debt-financed AI capex (an estimated 40% in 2027), higher yields and high expectations raise the risk of disappointment and an expectations reset.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disappointment in the Q3 earnings season, particularly for AI-sector companies.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic sweep would constrain fiscal spending and support bonds, and any signal of reduced long-end issuance at the 4 November refunding would compress yields.
tension_points.bear_case: A Republican sweep would price in more fiscal expansion and a higher term premium, and softening auction demand adds uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 3 November mid-term outcome and the 4 November Treasury refunding announcement.

tension_points.bull_case: EM central bank demand led by China, low speculative positioning and a softer USD ahead support a move to USD 4,700/oz.
tension_points.bear_case: USD strength, elevated real yields and rising bond yields are headwinds, and the negative gold-USD correlation has held gold back.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resilient USD and persistently elevated real yields.
